questions.question: A particle P rests in equilibrium on a smooth horizontal plane under three forces F1 = (3ci + 4cj) N, F2 = (-14i + 7j) N and F3 N. Find F3 in terms of c, i and j.
steps: Equilibrium means the resultant of the three forces is zero: F1 + F2 + F3 = 0.

questions.question: With c = 2 and F3 removed, F1 = 6i + 8j N and F2 = -14i + 7j N act on particle P. Find the angle between the direction of i and the direction of the resultant force on P.
steps: The resultant points into the second quadrant (negative i, positive j).

questions.question: With F3 removed and c = 2, the resultant force on particle P of mass m kg gives an acceleration of magnitude 8.5 m s^-2. Find m.
steps: Resultant force R = -8i + 15j N, with magnitude sqrt(64 + 225) = sqrt(289) = 17 N.
Newton's second law: R = ma, so 17 = 8.5m.

questions.question: A particle of weight W N lies at rest on a rough horizontal surface. A force of magnitude P N acts at angle alpha to the horizontal, pushing down onto the particle, where tan(alpha) = 4/3. The coefficient of friction is 1/4. Given that the particle does not move, show that P <= 5W/8.
steps: Vertically: R = W + P sin(alpha) = W + 4P/5.
Horizontally, the applied force component is P cos(alpha) = 3P/5, which must be balanced by friction F.
Friction limit: F <= mu R = (1/4)(W + 4P/5) = W/4 + P/5.

questions.question: A lift of mass 250 kg is raised vertically upwards with constant acceleration by a light inextensible cable with tension 3616 N. The floor exerts forces of 565 N on Alan and 226 N on Bhavana, who stand on the lift floor. Air resistance is negligible. Considering the forces acting on the lift only, find the acceleration of the lift.
steps: The children push the lift floor down with 565 + 226 = 791 N (Newton's third law).
Taking upwards as positive for the lift: 3616 - 250 x 9.8 - 791 = 250a.

questions.question: Alan stands on the floor of the lift accelerating upwards at 1.5 m s^-2. The floor exerts a force of 565 N on Alan. Find the mass of Alan.
steps: Forces on Alan: normal reaction 565 N upwards, weight m x 9.8 downwards.

questions.question: A bucket of mass 15 kg with a bag of cement of mass 25 kg moves vertically upwards with constant acceleration 0.2 m s^-2 on a vertical light inextensible cable. Air resistance is negligible. Find the tension in the cable.
steps: Treat the bucket and cement as one system of mass 15 + 25 = 40 kg.

questions.question: A box of tools of mass 12 kg is placed in the bucket. The bucket with the box moves vertically downwards with constant deceleration 0.1 m s^-2. Air resistance is negligible. Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the bucket and the box.
steps: Moving downwards with deceleration 0.1 means the acceleration is 0.1 m s^-2 upwards.
Forces on the box: normal reaction R upwards, weight 12 x 9.8 downwards.

questions.question: A tractor of mass 6 tonnes drags a block of mass 2 tonnes along rough horizontal ground by a horizontal light inextensible cable. The driving force of the tractor is 7400 N and its resistance is 200 N. The block has resistance R N. The tension in the cable is 6000 N and the tractor is accelerating. Find R.
steps: Block (2000 kg): tension 6000 forwards, resistance R backwards: 6000 - R = 2000 x 0.2.

questions.question: State how you have used the fact that the cable connecting the tractor and block is modelled as inextensible.
questions.answer: The tractor and block have the same acceleration, 0.2 m s^-2.
steps: An inextensible cable cannot stretch or shorten, so the two bodies move together.
Therefore the tractor and block have the same acceleration (0.2 m s^-2) in the working for part (a).

questions.question: A lift of mass m is raised by a light inextensible cable with tension 42mg/5. The lift and its contents, boxes P and Q, move upwards with acceleration 2g/5. Air resistance is negligible. Find, in terms of m, the combined mass of boxes P and Q.
steps: Let the combined mass of P and Q be M. Treat the lift and contents as one system of mass m + M.

questions.question: The lift moves upwards with acceleration 2g/5. During this motion the force exerted on box P by box Q is 14mg/5. Find, in terms of m, the mass of box P.
steps: Forces on P: upward force 14mg/5 from Q, weight pg downwards, where p is the mass of P.

questions.question: A boat, modelled as a particle, moves at constant speed in a straight line parallel to the riverbanks, pulled by two light ropes lying in a horizontal plane. Rope 1 has tension 500 N at 40 degrees to the direction of motion. Rope 2 has tension P N at alpha degrees to the direction of motion. The resistance to motion is a constant 900 N. Find the value of alpha.
steps: Constant speed in a straight line, so the resultant force is zero.
Perpendicular to the motion: 500 sin 40 = P sin alpha, so P sin alpha = 321.4.
Along the motion: 500 cos 40 + P cos alpha = 900, so P cos alpha = 516.98.
tan alpha = 321.4 / 516.98 = 0.6217, so alpha = 31.9 degrees (1 d.p.).

questions.question: The same boat is pulled at constant speed by rope 1 (500 N at 40 degrees) and rope 2 (P N at alpha degrees), with resistance 900 N. Find the value of P.
steps: From the components: P sin alpha = 321.4 and P cos alpha = 516.98.
